metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent removed all yellow highlights from the document by selecting all and applying No Fill highlight, then saved the file.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select all text, use Format menu, change font settings, apply character formatting, save files.
metadata.explanation: Chains highlight removal with a font change. Evaluator checks (1) no character highlights remain (0.5 pts) and (2) the default paragraph style in styles.xml or the most common text style in content.xml uses Arial font (0.5 pts). The original font is Cambria, so the initial state fails the font check. [Fixed: replaced truncated 16-char MD5 suffix df774da3e634fa76 with correct 32-char hash 582984f0118e076c9ea08b5f36393d3b; renamed functions from *_title_font to *_font; moved helper functions inline into the main getter. Fix 5: Getter now also checks loext:char-highlight-color (urn:org:documentfoundation:names:experimental:office:xmlns:loext:1.0) on all style:text-properties and text:span elements — this is the attribute LibreOffice Writer's Character Highlighting Color feature actually writes. Expanded no-highlight exclusion list to include 'none', '-1', '4294967295' (0xFFFFFFFF). Now has discriminative power for the highlight sub-goal and correct negative-control resistance.]
fix_history: Fix 1: Replaced truncated 16-char MD5 suffix 'df774da3e634fa76' with correct 32-char hash '582984f0118e076c9ea08b5f36393d3b' (computed from '6a33f9b9-0a56-4844-9c3f-96ec3ffb3ba2|4')
Fix 4: Moved helper functions (_load_odt, _has_char_highlights, _get_default_font, _get_widespread_font) inline into main getter to eliminate top-level naming violations

Fix 5: Added loext:char-highlight-color check to getter — LibreOffice Writer's Character Highlighting Color feature writes this LO-extension attribute (NS: urn:org:documentfoundation:names:experimental:office:xmlns:loext:1.0), not fo:background-color. Getter now iterates all style:text-properties AND text:span elements in content.xml for both fo:background-color and loext:char-highlight-color. Expanded no-highlight exclusion set to include 'none', '-1', '4294967295' (0xFFFFFFFF used by LO for 'no highlight'). This restores discriminative power for has_highlights and fixes negative-control resistance.
metadata.task_rationale: Hardened variation adding a global font change on top of highlight removal. Tests the agent's ability to change the document default font while also managing character highlighting.

scoring_breakdown.default_font_arial: 0.5 - Document default/widespread font is Arial (original was Cambria)

llm_judge_reasons: Fix 5 has been applied: getter now checks both 'fo:background-color' and 'loext:char-highlight-color' (the LibreOffice extension attribute used by Character Highlighting Color) in all style:text-properties (Pass 1) and text:span elements (Pass 2) in content.xml, restoring discriminative power for the highlight sub-goal.

Exclusion set for 'no highlight' values is now comprehensive: includes '', 'transparent', 'automatic', '#00000000', 'none', '-1', '4294967295' (0xFFFFFFFF) — covers all known LibreOffice representations of 'no highlight'.

Font detection correctly reads styles.xml default-style paragraph family (primary), falls back to 'Default Paragraph Style' named style, then to most-common font in content.xml automatic styles — appropriate hierarchy for detecting the document default font.
Metric correctly receives 'expected' as the rules dict (type='rule' framework behavior), uses expected.get('expected_font', 'Arial') and case-insensitive substring match — semantically sound.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 + 0.5) is appropriate for the two independent sub-goals. Default has_highlights=True (conservative) is correct.
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before getter runs — ensures file state is fresh and correct for file-based extraction.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The 'no_highlights: true' key in the expected rules dict is not directly used by the metric — the highlight sub-goal is evaluated purely from result.get('has_highlights', True). This is functionally correct but slightly inconsistent; consider documenting this pattern.

Minor: Named character styles with highlight colors defined in styles.xml are not checked (only content.xml is scanned). In practice LibreOffice stores Character Highlighting Color in content.xml automatic styles, so this is unlikely to cause issues.
